lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Welcome to World 22! Do you remember the old book from the tower? Today, we will walk down the stairs under the Tower of Messages. Down, down, down. Look! The walls are golden yellow. They're made of amber. This is the Amber Library. This library has a million books. Say it with me. This library has a million books. Wonderful! A million is a very big number. It's a thousand times a thousand! There are old books on every shelf. The librarian is a wise old owl. His name is Professor Quill. Here is a sign at the door. Let's read it together. "Welcome to the Amber Library. We have a million books, and every book has a story inside. Please speak softly. You can borrow three books at a time. If you need help, ask Professor Quill." Now, phonics. When we add e r to an action word, it means a person. Write, writer. Read, reader. Paint, painter. Teach, teacher. A writer writes books, and a reader reads them. Today, you are all readers! Let's go inside.

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, we're at the New Books Corner. Look at all these new books! When you see a new book, you can ask, What's it about? Say it with me. What's it about? Great! Then your friend answers, It's about a brave cat. It's about plus a thing or a person. It's about a robot. It's about a lost dog. Another good question is, What kind of book is it? It's an adventure story. It's a funny story. It's a mystery. Let's read the back cover of this book. "Whiskers is a small cat with a big heart. One night, a storm takes her family's boat away. Whiskers must sail across the sea alone to find it. Will she be brave enough?" So, what's it about? It's about a brave cat! What kind of book is it? It's an adventure story. Now, phonics. Some person words end in o r. Act, actor. Edit, editor. Narrate, narrator. Illustrate, illustrator. An illustrator draws the pictures in a book. O r sounds just like e r, so remember the spelling. Let's find a book!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Look at this poster on the library wall. There's a book signing event on Saturday. When you want to know about a book's writer, ask, Who wrote this book? Say it with me. Who wrote this book? Good! The answer can be short. A famous writer did. Nora Bell did. Did is a short way to say wrote. You can also ask about the pictures. Who drew the pictures? Her brother did. Let's read the poster together. "Book Signing Day! Come and meet Nora Bell, the writer of The Shy Dragon. She wrote more than twenty books for children. Her brother, Sam Bell, drew the pictures. Saturday at two o'clock in the Story Hall. Bring your favorite book!" So, who wrote The Shy Dragon? Nora Bell did. Who drew the pictures? Sam Bell did. Now, phonics. Some person words end in i s t. Art, artist. Cartoon, cartoonist. Novel, novelist. Guitar, guitarist. An artist makes art. A cartoonist draws cartoons. Let's talk about writers!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Do you have a favorite book? When you love a book, you want your friends to read it, right? You can say, You should read it. It's really funny. Say it with me. You should read it. It's really funny. Excellent! You should means it's a good idea for you. You can change the last word. It's really exciting. It's really sad, but beautiful. It's really scary! Add one more good point. The pictures are beautiful, too. And your friend can say, Thanks. I'll borrow it today. Here is a note from Birimo to Haru. Let's read it. "Haru, you should read Robot Chef. It's really funny. The robot tries to make a cake, but he uses salt, not sugar! The pictures are great, too. I put it on your desk. Birimo" Ha ha. Salt, not sugar! Now, phonics. Let's mix our person words. Dance, dancer. Create, creator. Violin, violinist. Sing, singer. Three end with an er sound. Violinist ends with ist. Let's recommend books to each other!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Welcome to the Book Talk Corner! In a book talk, you stand up and tell everyone about a book you like. Here's a good pattern. This book is about a lost robot. I like it because it's exciting. Say it with me. This book is about a lost robot. I like it because it's exciting. Great job! First, say what it's about. Then, say why you like it. Use because. I like it because the ending is happy. I like it because the robot is cute. Last, ask, Do you have any questions? Let's read Kiko's book talk card. "My book talk is about Beep, the Lost Robot. The writer is Tom Green. This book is about a little robot. He gets lost in a big city. Many people help him, and he finds his way home. I like it because it's exciting and warm. You should read it!" Very nice, Kiko. Now, phonics review. Writer. Actor. Artist. Explorer. Writers, actors, artists and explorers all have stories. Who will be the first speaker today?

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, we're in the Picture Book Room. Every story has a main character. The main character (しゅじんこう) is the most important person or animal in the story. Look at this book. It's The Shy Dragon by Nora Bell. The main character is a shy dragon. Say it with me. The main character is a shy dragon. Very good! Then you can say more. His name is Ember. He lives on a mountain. He's big, but he's very gentle. Let's read the first page of the book. "High on a quiet mountain, there lived a dragon named Ember. Ember was very big, and his wings were red like fire. But Ember was shy. When he saw people, he hid behind the rocks. He wanted a friend, but he was too shy to say hello." Poor Ember. Now, phonics. Today we meet a word family. The family name is act. Action. Actor. Active. Activity. They all have act inside. An actor acts. An active boy moves a lot. Who is the main character of your favorite book?

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, we will talk about what characters are like. We use words like brave, kind, smart, funny, shy and selfish. Look at this girl in The Magic Stone. Her name is Kai. She's brave and kind. Say it with me. She's brave and kind. Wonderful! To ask about a character, say, What's Kai like? What's she like? The answer is, She's smart and funny. Some characters are not so nice. He's a little selfish. A little makes it softer. Let's read about Kai. "Kai lived in a small village by the sea. She was not big or strong, but she was brave. One day, an old man fell into the river. Everyone was scared, but Kai jumped in and pulled him out. Later, she shared her lunch with a hungry dog. Kai was brave, and she was kind." What a hero! Now, phonics. Here's another word family. Invent. Invention. Inventor. Inventive. An inventor invents things. The thing is an invention. An inventive person has lots of new ideas. Let's describe some characters!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Adventure stories have a hero and a villain. The hero is the good main character. The villain (わるもの) is the bad character. Let's sort the characters in The Magic Stone. The hero is Kai. Rusty the fox helped her. And the villain? The villain wanted the magic stone. Say it with me. The villain wanted the magic stone. Great! Use wanted for what a character wished for. Use tried to for what a character wanted to do, but could not. Lord Grim tried to steal it. Let's read a page. "The magic stone glowed blue in the old temple. It kept the village safe from storms. Lord Grim wanted the stone for himself. One dark night, he tried to steal it. But Kai and Rusty were waiting. 'Not tonight, Lord Grim!' said Kai." Who is the hero? Kai. Who is the villain? Lord Grim. Now, phonics. Protect is our family word. Protection. Protector. Protective. Kai protected the stone. She is the protector of the village. A mother bird is very protective of her babies. Let's sort some characters!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, let's talk about our favorite characters. Ask your friend, Which character do you like the best? Then answer with a reason. I like the fox because he's clever. Say it with me. I like the fox because he's clever. Perfect! Because tells the reason. I like Kai because she never gives up. I like Ember because he's gentle. When your friend answers, react! Same answer? Me too! Different answer? Really? I like Kai! Here's a short page about Rusty the fox. "Rusty was a small red fox with a big smile. He was not strong, but he was clever. When Lord Grim's guards blocked the road, Rusty had an idea. He made a path of fallen leaves in a different direction. The guards followed it, and Kai got away!" What a clever fox. Now, phonics. Direct is a family word. Direction. Director. Directly. A director tells actors what to do. Go directly home means go straight home. And remember active from the act family. Which character do you like?

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, we will make character cards. A character card shows a picture and a few sentences about one character. Let's start with Mira from the book Mira the Inventor. This is Mira. She's a famous inventor. Say it with me. This is Mira. She's a famous inventor. Excellent! Then add what she likes, what she's like, and who her friends are. She likes building machines. She's smart and a little messy. Her best friend is a small robot named Bolt. Let's read Riko's character card. "Name: Mira. Book: Mira the Inventor. This is Mira. She's a famous inventor. She's ten years old. She likes building machines, and her room is full of tools. She's smart, but she's a little messy. Her best friend is a small robot named Bolt." Great card, Riko. Now, phonics review. Actor. Invention. Protective. Director. Remember the family names: act, invent, protect, direct. Endings tell us if the word is a person, a thing, or what someone is like. Let's make our cards!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, we will start reading The Shy Dragon. Every story has three parts. The beginning, the middle and the end. Today is the beginning. At the beginning, the dragon was alone. Say it with me. At the beginning, the dragon was alone. Great! At the beginning tells us when. It's the first part of the story. Then we learn more. Every day, he looked down at the village. Nobody knew his name. Let's read the beginning. "At the beginning of our story, Ember the dragon was alone. Every day, he sat on a rock and looked down at the village. He saw children playing and laughing. He wanted to play, too. But when he flew close, people ran away. So Ember stayed on his mountain. At night, he fell asleep under the stars, all alone." How does Ember feel? He feels lonely. Now, phonics. Listen. a SLEEP. a WAKE. a ROUND. a CROSS. We say the second part strongly. The first a is very short and weak, like uh. It's called the schwa. Asleep. Awake. Let's talk about the beginning of the story.

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we read the beginning of The Shy Dragon. Today, we will read the middle. The middle is where something happens. In the middle, he met a little girl. Say it with me. In the middle, he met a little girl. Very good! Storytellers use special words in the middle. One day. Suddenly. One day, a girl got lost in the snow. Suddenly, Ember heard a small voice. Suddenly makes the story exciting! Let's read. "One day, a big snowstorm came. Suddenly, Ember heard a small voice. 'Help! Is anyone there?' It was a little girl named Lulu. She was lost, and she was very cold. Ember wanted to help, but he was shy. What if she runs away, too? He took a deep breath and walked out from behind the rock." Oh, what will Lulu do? Now, phonics. Listen to the strong part. PEN cil. SEC ond. DRAG on. BUT ton. The second part is weak. The i in pencil and the o in second sound like uh. Let's talk about the middle of the story!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, we will finish The Shy Dragon. Let's read the end. At the end, they became friends. Say it with me. At the end, they became friends. Fantastic! At the end tells us the last part. You can also use finally. Finally, Ember took Lulu home. Became is the past of become. They became friends. And how about the ending? The ending was happy. Let's read the last page. "Lulu was scared at first. But then she saw Ember's kind eyes. 'Can you help me?' she asked. Ember nodded. He carried her on his back and flew over the mountain. Finally, they arrived at the village. The children cheered, and nobody ran away. At the end, Ember and Lulu became best friends." Hooray! I love happy endings. Now, phonics. PROB lem. CHIL dren. CIR cus. HAP pen. The strong part is first. The e in problem and the u in circus sound like a soft uh. Let's talk about the ending!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today is Story Time with Professor Quill. He reads a story, and stops at the exciting parts. When he stops, you can ask, What happened next? Say it with me. What happened next? Good! Then he answers, He found a door. Another great question is, Can you tell me more? Or just, And then? Good listeners ask questions like these. Professor Quill is reading The Secret Door. Let's read the first part. "Tom was playing in his grandma's garden. Suddenly, a white cat ran past him and jumped behind an old tree. Tom followed the cat. Behind the tree, there was something strange. It was a tiny green door with a golden handle." Oh! What happened next? He opened it very slowly. And then? Ha ha, we will find out later! Now, phonics. Listen to these story words. GI ant. LI on. PI lot. WIZ ard. The second part is weak. The a in giant sounds like uh. The o in lion and pilot sounds like uh, too. Let's ask good questions at Story Time!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, we will retell a story in thirty seconds. Retell means tell the story again in your own words. Use three steps. First. Then. At the end. Let's retell The Shy Dragon. First, the dragon was alone. Then, he met a girl. At the end, they became friends. Say it with me. First, the dragon was alone. Then, he met a girl. Great! At the end, they became friends. You can start with one sentence about the whole story. The story is about a shy dragon and a lost girl. Short and clear is best. Let's read Haru's retelling. "The story is about a shy dragon and a lost girl. First, Ember the dragon was alone on his mountain. Then, he met Lulu in a snowstorm. She was lost, so he carried her home. At the end, they became friends, and the villagers were happy." That's about thirty seconds. Perfect! Now, phonics review. a SLEEP. PEN cil. CHIL dren. GI ant. Strong, weak. Weak, strong. Ready? Let's start the timer!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Good readers think about how characters feel and why. Today, let's look at a sad scene in The Magic Stone. Why was Kai sad? She was sad because she lost her friend. Say it with me. She was sad because she lost her friend. Great! The feeling comes first. Then because and the reason. You can also give your own idea with I think. I think she felt lonely because Rusty was gone. Let's read the scene. "The storm was dangerous. The wind was loud, and the rain was cold. When the storm finally stopped, Kai looked around. Rusty was gone! She called his name again and again. Nobody answered. Kai sat down on a wet rock and cried. Without Rusty, the forest felt big and empty." Oh, poor Kai. How did she feel? Sad and lonely. Why? Because Rusty was gone. Now, phonics. Fame, famous. Danger, dangerous. Poison, poisonous. O u s makes a word that describes something. A poisonous mushroom is dangerous! Let's talk about feelings and reasons.

phonics.tipJa: adventure → adventurous（ぼうけんずきな）、mystery → mysterious（なぞの）、joy → joyous（よろこびに みちた）、envy → envious（うらやましがる）。しいん ＋ y は y を i に かえて ous。joy は o ＋ y なので そのまま。

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we used because to give a reason. Today, we will use so. So shows what happened next because of a feeling. He was scared, so he ran away. Say it with me. He was scared, so he ran away. Excellent! First the feeling, then so, then the action. Lulu was cold, so Ember made a fire. Now compare. He ran away because he was scared. He was scared, so he ran away. Same story, different order! Let's read a page from The Shy Dragon. "A long time ago, a hunter came to Ember's mountain. He had a loud horn and a big net. Ember was scared, so he ran away and hid in a deep cave. He stayed there for many days. After that day, Ember was afraid of people. That's why he was so shy." Now we know a mysterious secret about Ember! Now, phonics. Adventure, adventurous. Mystery, mysterious. Joy, joyous. Envy, envious. Mystery ends with y, so change y to i. Joy keeps its y. Let's connect feelings and actions with so!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Do you remember The Secret Door? Tom opened the tiny green door. Today, let's read what happened. When the bell rang, the door opened. Say it with me. When the bell rang, the door opened. Wonderful! When joins two events. When Tom stepped inside, the room was dark. You can put when in the middle, too. Everyone jumped when the clock struck twelve. Let's read. "When Tom stepped inside, the room was dark. Then he heard music. It was soft and magical. Suddenly, a little bell rang. When the bell rang, a second door opened, and warm light came out. Inside, there was a library full of glowing books!" Wait, everyone! Listen! Ding, ding. That's our library clock. Look! A door in the wall is opening! When the bell rang, the door opened, just like in the book! Now, phonics. Magic, magical. Music, musical. Nature, natural. A l makes a describing word. Let's look inside the secret room!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! We found a secret room behind the library wall. In the middle of the room, there's a big, old book. But it won't open. There's a golden lock on the cover. Professor Quill says, This is the Book That Won't Open. Nobody knows what's inside. Hmm. If we find the key, we can open the book. Say it with me. If we find the key, we can open the book. Great! If tells us the condition. If we look carefully, we will find a clue. If it rains, we will stay inside. You can ask, What will happen if we open it? Here's a note on the table. Let's read it. "This is the Book That Won't Open. Its key is hidden in a place full of feelings. If you find the key, you can open the lock. But be careful. The lock is not the only door to this book." Hmm, a place full of feelings? Now, phonics. Person, personal. Season, seasonal. Origin, original. Fame, famous. Let's look for clues. If we work together, we will find it!

phonics.tipJa: -ous と -al の まとめ: dangerous・mysterious（y を i に）・magical・natural（e を とる）。どれも ようすの ことば。おとは「アス」「アル」、つづりは ous と al。

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, we will make a Feelings Map. A Feelings Map shows how a character's feelings change from the beginning to the end. Let's make one for Lulu from The Shy Dragon. At first, she felt lonely. Later, she felt happy. Say it with me. At first, she felt lonely. Later, she felt happy. Very good! At first means at the beginning. Later means after some time. Then explain why. Her feelings changed because she found a friend. Let's read Kiko's Feelings Map. "Lulu's Feelings Map. At first, she felt lonely because she was lost in the snow. Then she felt scared because she saw a big dragon. Later, she felt safe because Ember was gentle. At the end, she felt happy because she had a new friend." Wow. Lonely, scared, safe, happy. Wait! Look at the back of Kiko's map. There's something shiny. It's a key! A place full of feelings. It was the Feelings Map! Now, phonics review. Dangerous. Mysterious. Magical. Natural. Let's make our maps!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, we will read a picture book with lines. Lines are the words characters say. In books, lines are inside quotation marks. They look like this. Two small marks at the start, and two small marks at the end. After the line, the book tells us who said it and how. Shouted the boy. Said the whale. Help! shouted the boy. Say it with me. Help! shouted the boy. Great! Shouted means said very loudly. Whispered means said very quietly. Let's read this page from Ken and the Whale. "The wave was huge, and Ken fell into the sea. 'Help!' shouted the boy. A big gray whale swam up from below. 'I'm here,' said the whale. 'Hold on to my fin.' Ken held on tight. When they reached the beach, Ken looked into the whale's kind eye. 'Thank you,' whispered the boy." Can you hear the different voices? Now, phonics and reading. Help, with an exclamation mark. Watch out, with an exclamation mark. Read them strongly! Who's there, with a question mark. Read it like a question. Let's read the lines together!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, we will play a game called Who Said It? I'll read a line, and you guess who said it. There's another way to write lines. The person comes first. She said, Thank you for saving me. Say it with me. She said, Thank you for saving me. Excellent! Notice the comma after said. Then the line starts with a capital letter. For questions, use asked. He asked, Can I be your friend? To ask about a line, say, Who said, Watch out? Rusty did. Let's read some lines from our books. "Line one: 'Where are you, Rusty?' Line two: 'Can I be your friend?' Line three: 'Thank you for saving me.' Line four: 'Wow! The stone is glowing!' Who said each line? Kai, Ember, Lulu, or Lord Grim?" Hmm, let's think. Kai asked, Where are you, Rusty? Ember asked, Can I be your friend? Lulu said, Thank you for saving me. Now, phonics and reading. Where are you, question mark. Wow, exclamation mark. Can you help me, question mark. Let's play Who Said It!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, we will read lines with feeling. The same words can sound very different. Listen. Oh no. That sounds sad. Oh no! That sounds surprised. Let's read it with feeling. Say it with me. Let's read it with feeling. Great! Books tell us how to read a line. Oh no! she cried sadly. Sadly means in a sad way. Oh no! he shouted in surprise. When you see sadly, read slowly and softly. When you see in surprise, read quickly and high. Let's read this short scene. "Mira's new robot fell off the table. Crash! 'Oh no!' she cried sadly. She picked up the pieces. Then Bolt rolled into the room with a box of tools. 'What happened?' asked Bolt. Mira smiled. 'We can fix it!' Two hours later, the robot stood up and waved. 'Hooray!' they shouted happily." How did Mira feel at first? Sad. And at the end? Happy! Now, phonics and reading. Oh no, exclamation. What happened, question. Hooray, exclamation. Let's read with feeling!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, some little children are coming to the library. You will read a picture book to them! Many stories start with four magic words. Once upon a time. Once upon a time, there was a little fox. Say it with me. Once upon a time, there was a little fox. Great! Remember to change your voice for the lines. Hello, said the fox. At the end, say, The end. Then ask, Did you like the story? Let's practice with The Fox and the Moon. "Once upon a time, there was a little fox. Every night, he looked up at the moon. One night, the moon came down to the hill. 'Who are you?' asked the moon. 'Hello,' said the fox. 'I'm Fox. I'm your biggest fan!' The moon laughed. 'Look out! You're standing on my light!' Fox jumped. 'Are you OK?' The moon smiled. 'I'm fine. Let's be friends.' The end." Now, phonics and reading. Who are you, question mark. Look out, exclamation mark. Are you OK, question mark. Hold the book so everyone can see. Let's practice!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Welcome to Story Theater! Today, four of you will act out The Shy Dragon. First, choose your roles. You can say, I'll be the narrator. You're Lulu. I'm Ember. The narrator tells the story, and the characters say their lines. Here's an important line. Who are you? asked the dragon. Say it with me. Who are you? asked the dragon. Very good! Ember is shy, so say it softly. Let's read our script. "Narrator: One snowy day, Lulu was lost on the mountain. Lulu: Help! Where are you, Mom? Narrator: A big dragon came out from behind a rock. Ember: Who are you? Lulu: I'm Lulu. I'm lost. Ember: Don't be scared. I'll take you home. Narrator: Ember flew Lulu home, and everyone cheered. Villagers: Hooray!" Before we start, remember. Look at the audience. Speak loudly and clearly. Read with feeling! Now, phonics and reading review. Help, exclamation. Where are you, question. Hooray, exclamation. Who are you, question. Let's start from the beginning. Lights, please!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! The big day is here. We have the key from the Feelings Map. Let's open the Book That Won't Open! Click. The golden lock opened. But wait. There's another lock inside with three empty lines. We need three words to open this book. Say it with me. We need three words to open this book. Great! There's a riddle under the lock. Let's read it. "Three words open this book. The first word is what Ember found on the mountain. The second word is what Kai showed in the storm. The third word is what Mira uses every day to make new things. Say the three words together, and say them with feeling." Hmm. What did Ember find? A friend. So, friendship! Give a reason. I think the first word is friendship because Ember found a friend. What did Kai show? She was brave. Courage! And Mira? She has lots of ideas. Imagination! Now, phonics review. Writer. Action. Pencil. Famous. OK, everyone. Let's say them together with feeling. Friendship! Courage! Imagination! Look! The book is opening!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! The Book That Won't Open is open now. But the pages are almost all blank! There's only one story inside, and it has no ending. Professor Quill says, The book wants a new ending from every reader. Let's read the story. "Sparky was a baby dragon. One night, a big wind blew him far away from his mountain. He landed in a quiet forest. He was cold and hungry, and he missed his mother. He looked up at the stars and made a wish. Then..." And that's the end of the page! So, it's your turn. What happens next? Haru has an idea. In my ending, the dragon flies home. Say it with me. In my ending, the dragon flies home. Wonderful! You can use maybe. Maybe his mother is waiting for him. You can use I think. I think the stars will show him the way. Then ask your friend, What's your ending? Now, phonics review. Illustrator. Invention. Awake. Magical. Every reader can be a writer, too. Let's imagine our endings!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, we will write Book Recommendation Cards. We'll put them on the library board, so other readers can find great books. A good card has four parts. Title. What it's about. The main character. And why someone should read it. You should read it because it's exciting. Say it with me. You should read it because it's exciting. Excellent! You can add your favorite part. My favorite part is the ending. Let's read Riko's card. "Title: The Shy Dragon. Writer: Nora Bell. It's about a shy dragon and a lost girl. The main character is Ember. He's big, but he's gentle and shy. My favorite part is the ending, because everyone cheers for Ember. You should read it because it's warm and exciting. Rating: five stars!" That's a great card. It makes me want to read the book again. Now, phonics review. Artist. Protector. Second. Adventurous. Hooray! Write your title in big letters, and write five to eight sentences. Let's make our cards!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today is our last tour of the Amber Library. Professor Quill will show us around one more time. Let's remember all the places. The New Books Corner, the Book Talk Corner, the Picture Book Room, the Story Hall and the secret room. In every room, we talked about books. What's it about? The main character is a shy dragon. At the beginning. In the middle. At the end. She was sad because she lost her friend. He was scared, so he ran away. Help! shouted the boy. At the end of our tour, we will say thank you. Thank you for everything, Professor Quill. Say it with me. Thank you for everything, Professor Quill. Beautiful! Here is a letter from Professor Quill. Let's read it. "Dear young readers, thank you for visiting my library. You read many stories, you talked about characters, and you even opened the Book That Won't Open. Now you are real readers and writers. Please come back anytime. The books will be waiting. Your friend, Professor Quill" Now, phonics review. Reader. Direction. Children. Natural. Who are you? Let's start our goodbye tour!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Welcome to the World 22 Grand Review! Today is the Book Festival in the big hall of the Amber Library. Everyone will present a favorite story. At the end of your talk, tell us the big idea of the story. That's the theme. This story is about friendship. I loved it! Say it with me. This story is about friendship. I loved it! Fantastic! Other themes are courage, family and kindness. In this world, you learned so much. What's it about? Who wrote it? You should read it. The main character is a shy dragon. He's big, but he's very gentle. At the beginning. In the middle. At the end. She was sad because she lost her friend. He was scared, so he ran away. When the bell rang, the door opened. If we find the key, we can open the book. Help! shouted the boy. Here is the festival program. Let's read it. "Book Festival Program. Part one: Book talks. Part two: Story Theater, The Shy Dragon. Part three: Readers read their new story endings. Part four: A goodbye song from the little children." Now, phonics review. Writer. Narrator. Active. Giant. Mysterious. Help! You are wonderful readers. Let the festival begin!
